title: ix months into the Iran war, what has Trump accomplished? #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
Six months after the United States and Israel launched military action against Iran, the conflict shows no sign of coming to an end.
 
As Washington turns its focus to economic pressure, Tehran remains defiant - with the Strait of Hormuz seen as key leverage.
 
The uncertainty keeps economies and markets volatile, pushing up prices around the world and straining international relations.
 
A conflict that US President Donald Trump said would last a few weeks has now lasted half a year, so where do we go from here and when might the war end?

description:
Today, NHS bosses have warned of chaos in ADHD and autism care as costs spiral and unregulated private providers capitalise on the huge demand for help.

Health editor Hugh Pym is in the studio to describe what’s been going on in the NHS, and why bosses are warning about what’s going on behind the scenes as requests for ADHD and autism diagnoses rise.

And, what more have we learned about the unannounced visit of CIA chief John Ratcliffe to Moscow earlier this week? The Economist’s Washington bureau chief Shashank Joshi unpacks the reports around possible motives for his visit, including warning Russia against attacking NATO members. author: BBC News
description:
China has warned there is a "high risk" that a lake which formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may breach its banks, causing a second flood downstream.
 
The warning comes after Wednesday's deadly flash flood in the same area which has killed more than 500.
 
Scientists say it was triggered by the collapse of a mountain glacier into a river.

description:
Xbox chief executive Asha Sharma says the gaming giant needs to be "thinking about" affordability for its next-generation console, amid a "crisis" in computing prices.
 
Speaking exclusively to the BBC's Laura Cress at Gamescom in Cologne, she said rising hardware costs partly driven by AI spending mean firms need to find ways to make gaming affordable.
 
She also revealed gamers will soon be able to get digital versions of many of the physical games they currently own, potentially meaning their old games can be played on future Xbox consoles without having to put a disc in a drive.

author: BBC News
description:
The Netflix show Emily in Paris has been lauded by French President Emmanuel Macron, who presented its creator, Darren Star, with the prestigious Légion d’Honneur last year. 

“You make France shine across the world,” Macron said.   

Many critics disagree. The programme, about a hapless American marketing executive living a glamorous and romantic fantasy in the French capital, is due to return for its sixth and final season later this year. 

Some Parisians have complained that the series is full of cliches. And they worry that the tourism boost created by the show is changing the city they live in.   

How do blockbuster TV series and iconic films reshape our cities, for better or worse? 

The Global Story host, Tristan Redman, heads to the fifth arrondissement, while producers Hannah Moore and Xandra Ellin get the picture in London and New York.

Many of these attacks are not widely reported on.

author: BBC News
description:
Norway's King Harald V has died at the age of 89, after he was taken to hospital last week for treatment for a rare blood condition.
 
The palace in Oslo said he passed away peacefully at 06:35 local time (04:35GMT) on Friday at the national hospital in the capital. 
 
The royal flag on the roof of the palace has been lowered to half-mast.
 
Harald was Norway's first king born in the country since the 14th Century, and he spent 35 years on the throne. He will be succeeded by his son Haakon.
